subject: biochemistry
title: RNA transcription, post-transcriptional processing, and spliceosome defects

steps.tx: Eukaryotic **transcription** is orchestrated by three distinct nuclear RNA polymerases. RNA polymerase I synthesizes 28S, 18S, and 5.8S ribosomal RNAs. RNA polymerase II transcribes messenger RNAs and microRNAs, but is selectively inhibited by alpha-amanitin from death cap mushrooms. RNA polymerase III produces transfer RNAs and 5S ribosomal RNA. Initiation requires TATA-binding protein and general transcription factors assembling at core promoter elements.
steps.say: Eukaryotic transcription utilizes three nuclear RNA polymerases. RNA polymerase one synthesizes ribosomal RNAs, RNA polymerase two generates messenger RNAs and is poisoned by alpha-amanitin, while RNA polymerase three produces transfer RNAs. Promoter assembly requires TATA-binding protein.

steps.tx: Primary mRNA transcripts undergo essential **post-transcriptional** modifications within the nucleus prior to export. A 7-methylguanosine cap is added to the 5-prime end to ensure ribonuclease protection and ribosome recognition. Polyadenylate polymerase attaches a 200-nucleotide poly-A tail to the 3-prime terminus. The **spliceosome**, composed of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins, precisely excises non-coding introns at invariant GU-5-prime and AG-3-prime donor-acceptor splice junctions.
steps.say: Primary transcripts require three nuclear processing steps: addition of a 5-prime 7-methylguanosine cap, 3-prime polyadenylation by poly-A polymerase, and spliceosomal removal of non-coding introns at GU and AG consensus junctions by small nuclear ribonucleoproteins.

steps.tx: Primary pre-mRNA undergoes 5-prime 7-methylguanosine capping and 3-prime polyadenylation in the nucleus. The spliceosome then excises non-coding introns at invariant splice junctions prior to export. Primary mRNA transcripts undergo essential post-transcriptional modifications within the nucleus prior to export. A 7-methylguanosine cap is added to the 5-prime end to ensure ribonuclease protection and ribosome recognition.

steps.tx: Mutations altering consensus splice sites cause severe human **pathology**. Splicing mutations in the beta-globin gene disrupt normal exon assembly, generating aberrant transcripts and severe beta-thalassemia major. In systemic lupus erythematosus, autoantibodies target **snRNPs** (anti-Smith antibodies), directly impeding spliceosome assembly. Alternative splicing enables a single pre-mRNA to yield distinct tissue-specific protein isoforms, including membrane-bound versus secreted immunoglobulins.
steps.say: Splice site mutations cause aberrant exon inclusion, underlying beta-thalassemia. Anti-Smith antibodies in lupus specifically target snRNPs, impairing spliceosomal machinery. Alternative splicing allows a single gene to encode diverse tissue-specific isoforms.

steps.tx: Therapeutic modulation of RNA splicing represents a major **pharmacological** breakthrough. Nusinersen, an antisense oligonucleotide, binds pre-mRNA of the SMN2 gene, forcing exon 7 inclusion to restore functional motor protein in spinal muscular atrophy. Duchenne muscular dystrophy is treated by antisense morpholinos that induce exon-skipping to restore an in-frame dystrophin reading frame, converting fatal muscular dystrophy into a milder Becker phenotype.
steps.say: Therapeutic splice modulation uses antisense oligonucleotides like nusinersen to promote exon inclusion in spinal muscular atrophy, or exon-skipping morpholinos to restore in-frame dystrophin reading frames in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
